feedback: Sue's confession follows the strongest concrete contradiction I noticed: she invented someone pouring beside her when the service record put the pour in the kitchen. It explains why her glass handling required an invented witness rather than merely admitting another secret. Her ownership-advice exposure was already established, and the bottle-to-glass method was available before voting. The confession supplies her exact act and separate visit, but those are confirmations of a viable inference rather than a new technique or hidden evidence. Emotionally the appeal to Mona works because their relationship appeared throughout. It feels earned as a solution, though I still found the pre-vote differentiation weaker than the method itself and wrongly weighted Elle's portable cover and financial denial.
